newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil police to investigate Central Bank - report.
newsitem.headline: Brazil police to investigate Central Bank - report.

text.p: Police will investigate the alleged failure of Brazil's Central Bank to obey a court order to suspend liquidation of a bank and trading house, the private CBN radio network reported on Saturday.
The ruling involves Banco Interunion, which went into liquidation under a Central Bank decree on December 30.

On Friday a judge suspended the liquidation, but the Central Bank would not accept delivery of the court order, saying it had to be received in person by Central Bank President Gustavo Loyola, who was away in Sao Paulo, newspapers said.
Annoyed by the bank's refusal to acknowledge the order, the judge then began legal proceedings against Loyola for disobedience, the Estado de Sao Paulo newspaper said.

The federal attorney's office subsequently asked federal police to open an investigation to see if the Central Bank had deliberately ignored the court order, CBN radio said. It said Loyola may be questioned by police next week.
O Globo newspaper said the Central Bank chief could face arrest if the bank was proven to have acted in bad faith.
A Central Bank spokesman said he had only heard of the investigation through the media and reiterated that Loyola had not yet received any court order.
Federal police officials were unavailable for comment.
